newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish nurses strike still threatened - media.
newsitem.headline: Irish nurses strike still threatened - media.

text.p: Talks between health service employers and nurses union leaders, aimed at averting a strike, were adjourned after five-and-a-half hours on Wednesday night, Irish media reported on Thursday.
There has been no indication that the dispute will be settled, reports said, adding that Labour court talks are due to resume later on Thursday.

Irish nurses have threatened their first ever strike starting next Monday if their demands, which include early retirement at 55, better terms for staff nurses and those entering the profession and bonuses for those with additional qualifications, are not met.
They have already rejected a 50 million punt government offer.

Irish health minister Michael Noonan says he cannot afford any more than what is on offer and is also worried that he could trigger a further round of public sector pay claims if he meets the nurses' demands.
The Labour Court, a state funded arbitration body, invited health service employers and nurses' union leaders into exploratory talks on Tuesday last in a bid to avert the nationwide strike.

If the strike goes ahead it is expected to lead to the cancellation of routine hopsital admissions and out-patient appointments and a withdrawal from non-nursing support work and administrative duties.

There is also growing uncertainty about the extent of emergency cover that will be provided in Dublin hospitals as local strike committees are reported to be reluctant to provide the levels of cover agreed by unions at national level.
